about: MOSS-TTS-Nano CPU/local viability measurements (Phase 1B). Machine: 4-core Xeon 2.1 GHz, 15.7 GB RAM, no GPU.

model_size_mb.note: ONNX exports are fp32 (external .data weights); PyTorch weights fp32 .bin/.safetensors. Params: ~0.1B TTS + ~20M codec.

cold_start.method: sync; echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches; then start the worker and send one request (#25 «Где вы живёте?», female FLEURS reference, WeText ON)

onnx_repo_runtime.note: the repo's onnx_tts_runtime.py imports torch + torchaudio (reference-audio loading/resampling), so this RSS includes torch

onnx_sessions_only_torch_free.note: ort_cpu_runtime.OrtCpuRuntime alone: all 8 ONNX sessions (prefill, decode, local ×3, codec encode/decode/decode_step)

cold_start.first_ever_load_note: the very first PyTorch-worker start in this environment took 14.5 s (WeTextProcessing compiles/caches its FST grammars on first use)

realtime_on_this_cpu: No. Median RTF 1.35–1.43 (PyTorch) and 1.91–2.00 (ONNX Runtime CPU): generation is slower than playback, so streamed audio starts in ~0.6–1.1 s but would underrun during playback without buffering. The README's '4-core CPU realtime' claim did not hold on this 2.1 GHz Xeon.
streaming: Both official runtimes stream (PyTorch NanoTTSService.synthesize_stream; ONNX codec decode_step session). Time-to-first-audio measured per synthesis (results.json first_audio_s).

on_device_path.browser: Official: OpenMOSS/MOSS-TTS-Nano-Reader @ c3b2333 runs the full ONNX stack as a browser extension on onnxruntime-web (WASM, SIMD, multi-threaded), no local server. Its JS runtime states WeTextProcessing is NOT available in-browser (robust normalization only) — which avoids the Cyrillic→Chinese-WeText number problem measured here. Not executed in this benchmark (no browser run).
on_device_path.android: No official Android build found. Credible route: the same ONNX graphs on ONNX Runtime Mobile (Java/Kotlin API) + SentencePiece for the text tokenizer; ~0.73 GB fp32 assets and ~1.3 GB RSS (torch-free, measured here) are heavy for phones — quantization would be needed. Community ports exist on modelscope.cn (INT8 ONNX: linlinkj/MOSS-TTS-Nano-100M-INT8, hzp2000itb/moss_nano_tts_onnx_100M_INT8; MNN: ZhangZes/MOSS-TTS-Nano-MNN; AXERA NPU; MLX) — unofficial, not tested here.
on_device_path.text_frontend: Tokenizer is SentencePiece (portable). Server-side text normalization uses WeTextProcessing (pynini FSTs) — not portable to browser/mobile as-is, and misroutes Russian to its Chinese grammar.
on_device_path.output_format: 48 kHz stereo (2-channel) — larger buffers than needed for speech on device.
